title: I guess this is gonna be it.

posts.author: Poryg
posts.body:
Two times I left, two times I came back. This time, the community is leaving us. So I guess this is my last farewell. Farewell both to the community and to the username that has made me company through the internet since 2009. If I ever come to the guild, it won't be under this name.
I've been an on-and-off lurker since MZ came out, so for those who are too recent to know me: I came here in 2017. As a child, I dealt with Don Miguel's rips of RM2k/2k3 and back then, we had no tutorials, so I came here a seasoned eventer. However, the combination of MV being open-source, limitations of publicly available plugins and too much time on my hands have pushed me to learn programming. I was always happy to help if the problem was interesting or the person was willing to learn, but I didn't like to provide full solutions as much unless they were simple. I also once tried to develop my own engine for MV, but it ended up being a painful lesson on the importance of having backups. Overall, it was a nice journey even if my achievements are limited. It's a pity it all ends like this - an abrupt end. But to be honest, as sad as I may be, I can't say I'm at all surprised.
My relationship with RPG Maker began to turn south after something I've never been able to comprehend: the MV 1.6.0 public beta and its aftermath. That version brought new nwjs, new PIXI and new bugs in the editor (where the bugs came from, that's a mystery, but I digress). The public beta was meant to find and eliminate the bugs before official release. I was one of the participants. I reported bugs, some of which were quite serious. Imagine my shock when I saw a 1.6 official release and immediately replicated every single bug I'd reported. The community backlash was brutal and resulted in the 1.6 being immediately pulled out. Eventually, we got a proper 1.6. But there were no new features, only better nwjs and PIXI. Instead of new features, we got MZ - something that, for the most part, MV should have been, but the "update" would cost 78€. So, that was when I bid farewell to my active role in the RPG Maker community and began to lurk in the shadows. And from the shadows, it was interesting to watch the community's sentiment slowly shift - 6 years ago, people were looking forward to the new maker and I was one of the few voices of negativity. Now, the community shows the a lot of the same disillusion as me back then.
I've seen people come, seen people go, seen people get banned, seen people die, seen GGG achieve two spectacular failures, seen the inception of AI... and now, I'm seeing the end of an era and a huge chapter in my life. Thanks to everyone. Thanks to the community for all the good and all the bad. Thanks to the admins for the community projects - they were fun. Thanks to mods, former and present, for your work. Thanks to Kadokawa for RPG Tsukuru - it was a great learning experience. And thanks to GGG for the most sensible thing I've seen them do since releasing Unite: changing the TOU of the RTP and DLC and allowing their use in any engine outside of RPG Maker.
And remember: the end of one chapter is the beginning of another one.
